long_biography.plain_text:
A former teacher inspired healthcare entrepreneur Randall Pittman's $6 million commitment to Michigan State University. He and his wife, Mary, pledged the money in 2002 to renovate the economics department's historic home, requesting the name Marshall-Adams Hall in honour of Walter Adams. Pittman had studied under Adams and earned degrees in political science and business administration at the university.

The couple also assembled a substantial collection of paintings by American landscape artist Russell Chatham. Built over roughly twelve years with the help of specialist dealers, it supplied 23 works for a 2008 retrospective at the Dennos Museum Center. That exhibition brought paintings from different stages of Chatham's career together for public viewing.
